Playwriting Group
description: All playwrights welcome! Whether playwriting is new to you or you're already an accomplished playwright, come join this on-going bi-weekly writers' group. We'll spend our time focusing on our writing, but with that magical element of doing so within the presence of others. Come discover the amazing experience of writing within the context of a group. Bring your computer, notebook, iPad, or whatever you like to use for writing. We share resources, discuss our goals and challenges, even provide feedback, but the primary focus of the group is to work on your own play! We'll do a check-in/discussion at the beginning of the meeting, then write in silence, and check-out at the end of our session. Contact Kimberly for the location and to answer any questions you may have. Category: Literary, Theater / Theatre

title: Amelia Zitoun, Cello, with Minhye Choi, Piano
description: Music in the Mountains welcomes rising cello star Amelia Zitoun, joined by pianist Minhye Choi, for an afternoon recital of music Zitoun loves. The program features Beethoven's Sonata No. 4 in C Major, Op. 102, No. 1; Debussy's Sonata for Cello and Piano in D Minor; Janáček's Pohádka (Fairy Tale); and Britten's Cello Sonata in C, Op. 65, written for legendary cellist Mstislav Rostropovich., , Zitoun won the Gold Medal at the 2023 Stulberg International String Competition and advanced to the round of twelve at the 2026 George Enescu International Competition. She has appeared as a soloist with the Milwaukee Symphony Orchestra, the Madison Symphony Orchestra and the San José Chamber Orchestra, and currently studies at the Colburn School with Clive Greensmith. Choi is a collaborative pianist at the Colburn Conservatory and Academy of Music and has performed throughout Europe, Korea and the United States.

title: Lost in Place Hank Meals Presentation
description: LOST IN PLACE - A PRESENTATION ABOUT OUR REGION’S COLORFUL, DESCRIPTIVE & USEFUL, PLACE NAMES, by Hank Meals , A lively slide show presentation about our tongue tripping topography., Who hasn’t been awed by the simplicity, elegance, mystery and humor of place names found in the Sierra Nevada? Names like Hornswoggle Creek, Shenanigan Flat, Starvation Bar and Sugarloaf. Naming places allowed us to navigate in the landscape and names for places were probably among the very first words., , Over the past fifty years Hank has photographed and researched many of these places. Among the places he’s visited are Gold Lake, Gates of the Antipodes, Cut-Eye Fosters Bar, Timbuctoo, Cloud Splitter, Cherokee Creek, Coyote Diggings, Depot Hill, German Bar, China Flat, Brandy City, Sweetland, Smartsville, Grizzly Hill, Sucker Flat and Native American Ravine. The relatively new field of experimental geography, as practiced by Hank, definitely includes humor. Whether you’re an artist, writer, walker, or want to be, you will enjoy this presentation.
